A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Seek-CAD and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched, including the retained appendix examples and v3's added Appendix A.11.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation and refinement experiments on 500 CAD models, component ablations on 200 models, and qualitative generation and editing results.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds CAD-Llama comparisons, feedback-quality and complexity analyses, and generation results on 300 DeepCAD test models.

M1.justification: The stated inference refinement cap changes from two rounds to one in Figure 1's caption and Section 5. The DeepSeek/RAG/SVF pipeline and SSR/CapType representation remain unchanged. Section 3.1 and the diagrams still specify two rounds, leaving the implemented stopping limit inconsistently documented.

E1.justification: v3 adds generation evaluation using a DeepCAD-only retrieval corpus and test set, testing the simpler SE setting. v1 already compared DeepCAD's dataset characteristics in Appendix A.2 but did not report this generation experiment. The text-to-CAD task and principal SSR dataset remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds the fine-tuned CAD-Llama baseline, which v1 cited but did not evaluate. The existing 3D-PreMise and CADCodeVerify feedback substitutions remain. The new DeepCAD comparison uses those same two comparators without CAD-Llama.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends the evaluation design: 4,000 DeepCAD retrieval models with 300 disjoint test models, feedback categorization over 500 samples with human checks, and complexity strata of 0–30, 31–70, and at least 71 commands. It also reports a one-round default instead of two, although conflicting specifications remain. Existing metrics and original evaluation sets are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds analyses of feedback usefulness and potential harm, performance versus command-sequence complexity, and robustness to replacing the SSR retrieval/evaluation setting with DeepCAD. These address substantial additional questions beyond v1's retained refinement-round sweep, component ablations, and appendix case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. Both report means or point estimates. The added feedback-category frequencies are empirical results, rather than a change in uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original numerical entries in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. v3 adds CAD-Llama results, feedback frequencies of 88.2% labeled helpful and 11.8% unsure, complexity-dependent results, and DeepCAD comparisons, including Seek-CAD CD of 0.1811. The DeepCAD values describe a new setting, not a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: The retrieval, refinement, SSR, CapType, and appendix prompt-construction formulations are substantively retained. Equation 12 changes a code-variable symbol from cj to sj without changing its meaning. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical argument is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction shift the motivating gap from closed-source cost and deployment restrictions to insufficient use of CoT. The explicit first-investigation claim for combined visual/CoT feedback is softened. The central training-free Seek-CAD, SSR, and dataset contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of the CAD-Llama fidelity/novelty trade-off, complexity-related accuracy loss and novelty gains, feedback usefulness, and applicability beyond the SSR evaluation setting. It also explains why correct feedback may still exceed the 32B model's capabilities and why CapType's inaccessible primitives prevent certain corrections.

D1.justification: The introduction changes a planned future dataset release into a reported public release with a repository access link. This availability statement is supported by the PDF but was not externally verified. Hardware, model quantization, inference parameters, RAG software details, prompts, and appendix interfaces are otherwise essentially retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds ReCAD and WHUCAD, acknowledging reinforcement-learning approaches and WHUCAD's comparable complex-feature coverage. References including BRep-BERT, SketchGen, and Wang et al.'s visual-feedback Text-to-CAD work are removed. The principal positioning against 3D-PreMise and CADCodeVerify remains.

P1.justification: There are targeted abstract, introduction, and discussion revisions, additional experimental subsections, updated affiliations, and removal of the standalone conclusion. Appendix A.11 is added. Most method explanations and existing appendix prose remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the ICLR template, expands Table 1 with a strategy column and CAD-Llama row, adds Tables 4–6, and relocates existing displays. Appendix Figure 15 enlarges the existing pipeline modules rather than presenting a new method. The original figures and qualitative galleries are retained.

improvement.justification: The added CAD-Llama and DeepCAD comparisons, feedback and complexity analyses, and reported dataset access strengthen validation and usability beyond v1. The gain is limited by sparse CAD-Llama setup and human-review details, plus the inconsistent one-versus-two-round specification. These additions improve the evidence without resolving the paper's main reproducibility and evaluation limitations.
